01 Who we are

Technology gets the event started.
People make it work.

ITS Event Support is the student-facing technical team helping campus events run smoothly—from the first microphone check to the final cable packed away.

You’ll work alongside professional ITS staff, event organizers, presenters, and other students. You don’t need to arrive as an expert. Bring curiosity, reliability, and a willingness to learn; training helps you build the rest.

Curious

Ask how systems work and keep learning through real assignments.

Calm

Think clearly, communicate early, and stay composed when plans shift.

Connected

Support people across campus with professional, attentive service.

02 What we do

Every assignment has a rhythm.

Prepare carefully. Stay present. Finish strong. Event Support turns the moving parts of campus events into a clear, repeatable workflow.

01 Before

Set the room for success.

Prepare, connect, test, and verify microphones, speakers, displays, and conferencing equipment.

  • Review the event plan
  • Run signal checks
  • Confirm presenter needs
02 During

Stay one step ahead.

Assist presenters, operate assigned systems, communicate with the team, and troubleshoot in real time.

  • Monitor the room
  • Support transitions
  • Respond with composure
03 After

Leave it ready for next time.

Break down, organize, document issues, and reset equipment so the next team can begin confidently.

  • Pack with care
  • Report equipment issues
  • Reset the space
03 What you’ll gain

Skills that travel with you.

This role welcomes students from different majors. The strongest tool you can bring is the desire to learn how technology and people work together.

01

Master AV technology

Learn the fundamentals of microphones, mixers, speakers, projection systems, and live audio and video.

Technical fluency
02

Build your network

Collaborate with faculty, staff, organizers, students, and campus guests through real working relationships.

Professional exposure
03

Explore live production

Build a foundation that may lead to further learning in cameras, live switching, and production coordination.

Creative pathways
04

Grow professional skills

Practice communication, troubleshooting, decision-making, teamwork, and composure during live events.

Career readiness

Beyond the equipment

Your next connection could start at your next event.

Every assignment is an opportunity to practice how you listen, explain, collaborate, and solve problems with people across the university.

Professional communication Campus-wide perspective Confidence with new people Real working relationships

Connections grow naturally through the work. The role does not guarantee referrals, internships, or personal access to visiting speakers.

04 Your growth path

Start with the fundamentals.
Keep moving forward.

Your path develops through supervised practice, demonstrated readiness, and the opportunities available to the team.

  1. 1

    Foundations

    Learn the setup

    Identify equipment, manage cables, test microphones, and understand setup and breakdown.

  2. 2

    Live support

    Work the event

    Assist presenters, operate basic AV systems, communicate clearly, and troubleshoot common issues.

  3. 3

    Ownership

    Take the lead

    After training, handle more complex setups or independently manage assigned technical responsibilities.

  4. 4

    Explore

    See what’s next

    Subject to training and departmental opportunities, gain exposure to cameras, switching, recording, or technical direction.

i

A pathway, not a promise. Advanced production opportunities depend on departmental needs, available training, and coordination with LMU teams responsible for media production.

05 Life behind the scenes

A shift can change with the calendar.
The learning never stops.

On event days, you’re part of the live experience. Between assignments, scheduled work may include preparation, training, and equipment checks.

8:30

Team check-in

Review the room, schedule, and technical plan with the event lead.

9:00

Line check

Test inputs, presentation content, room audio, and conferencing systems.

10:00

Doors open

Welcome presenters, monitor assigned systems, and stay ready for changes.

11:30

Reset & report

Pack equipment, note issues, and leave the space ready for what comes next.
